RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 5

An all-women panel choosing a woman over another woman is not evidence of sex discrimination against you. Both finalists shared your sex, so sex can't explain why one was preferred. Panel composition alone tells you little — it may simply reflect the department's staffing. Raising it would likely read as an unfounded accusation and weaken your credibility on the point that actually matters.

That real issue is substantive: on paper you have the stronger academic record (completed PhD, six papers, four years teaching), and the university owes you a written explanation. Send a formal written reminder citing the relevant rules and any deadline, and ask specifically how the criteria were weighted and how "industry experience" was scored. Escalate to an ombudsman if ignored.
